items.title: Victorian socialists’ sugar may smuggle poison into Parliament
paras: Young, articulate, black-shirt and keffiyeh-clad poll workers offering (ideological) free stuff for votes could propel the socialists into the Victorian Parliament.
‘Tax the billionaires, help fight One Nation’s racism, put politicians on workers’ wages!’ were relentlessly yapped into voters’ ears on the way to vote.
Victorian socialists’ black shirts would start in the car park and walk alongside unsuspecting voters offering dollops of sugar to disguise their political poison.

With most Australians, particularly young people, completely ignorant of politics these mantras were as seductive as the siren songs Odysseus and his men encountered on their journey home from the horrors of the Trojan wars.
Many willingly submitted to the pitch. Most over 40 understand reality and gave them short shrift.
Asked to provide examples of nations where socialism had worked, my interlocutor cited the Nodic countries.
I countered that they had massive sovereign wealth funds thanks to North Sea oil.
He said Australia also had massive natural resources. Trouble is the climate-obsessed socialists would never let us use them.
Indeed, a sovereign wealth fund from our nation’s endowment would be the way to provide gold-plated healthcare, pensions, and public infrastructure.
Typical of all socialists, my polling booth companion rejects my arguments about the failures of the Soviet Union – ie the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR).
I postulated that the reason the guns and gulags were needed is because people would not willingly give up their rights to private property.
A young Liberal at my booth tells me there are two socialist clubs on his Melbourne campus.
This is my second Victorian election. In 2022 the socialists were a disorganised rabble.
In 2026, they are well-drilled in campaign tactics. Bright young people swarming the booths coached with potent lines.

I’ve seen the same campaign strategy being executed brilliantly at three different polling booths – Seabrook at Point Cook, the Caroline Springs Library, and at the First Milleara Scout Hall in Premier Ben Carroll’s electorate of Niddrie in Melbourne’s west.
The irony of ‘fight One Nation’s racism’ was lost on the young socialist at Seabrook wearing his ‘Free Palestine’ T-shirt as scores of Indian and African migrants rushed the orange shirts.

Migrants in their droves, many wearing hijabs, grasping One Nation how to vote cards, was something I also observed when staffing a polling booth at Parafield Gardens in Adelaide’s northern suburbs last March.
The left’s tropes no longer work on an electorate that is yearning for change.
That yearning transcends ethnic boundaries and defies the left’s ongoing attempts to divide us by race.
But for the young unable to afford a house, taxing the billionaires sounds like a great plan.
I asked my black-shirted friend how many billionaires there were in Australia and how much the socialists would have to tax them to pay for utopia.
He didn’t know and said he would never be able to convince me, so it was pointless discussing the detail.
He said taxing the billionaires was a slogan for their agenda ensure all rich people paid more taxes.
Now there may be an argument for increasing taxes on the mega-wealthy or closing some loopholes, but my rejoinder that we should be careful what we wish for was lost on the young idealist.
The socialists have no idea how wealth is created – they think workers create wealth.
Workers certainly contribute but without an entrepreneur who takes the risk of putting up capital to employ people to produce things, there is no wealth.
Socialists don’t understand that if the rich are soaked, there will be less capital to invest in creating jobs for workers, fewer taxes paid, and therefore less government services.
They don’t understand Margaret Thatcher’s dictum about what happens when socialists run out of other peoples’ money.
Somehow in their minds money is like a magic pudding – you can keep dolling it out and supernaturally the cake replaces itself.
Socialism’s atheism seemingly has a strong faith dimension – like Jesus and the feeding of the 5,000 with five loaves and two fishes.
There should, of course, always be a debate in civil society about fair wages and conditions but that is not what the socialists are about.
But socialists go beyond this and foment toxic envy at those who have succeeded. It’s why they get on with radical Islam – another worldview that promotes a victim mentality.
Gaza’s Islamic radicals would throw the socialists’ gay mates off buildings.
The only thing in common the socialists have with Middle East politics is the enemy of my enemy is my friend.
The red-green alliance is united in its hatred of a common enemy – Western Civilisation.
Given that Australia was made great by its Western inheritance, political Islam and socialism, in my view, are an existential threat.
That’s why slick young socialists staffing Victorian polling booths are a worry.

The price of liberty is eternal vigilance. Our failure to meet the socialist challenge, particularly at a time when young people have been shut out of the Australian dream because of the mismanagement of successive Labor and Liberal politicians, is allowing toxic ideas to metastasise.
Ideas have consequences. History has resoundingly proven that socialist ideas lead to dystopia when the money inevitably runs out.
Our failure to counter bad ideas will condemn us to repeat the mistakes of the past.
Lyle Shelton is National Director of the Family First and is in Melbourne this week working on the party’s campaign.

items.title: Gerry Harvey: a recession is inevitable for Australia
paras: In the wake of this week’s shock inflation data and last week’s jump in unemployment to a five-year high, Harvey Norman’s chairman Gerry Harvey believes that a recession is now almost certain, and it is just a matter of how long it will last.
Households and businesses have already dealt with five rate hikes this year, taking the official cash rate to an 18-year high.

Last week’s worse-than-expected rise in the nation’s unemployment rate to 4.9% was well above the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) forecast and had financial markets tipping a rate cut in the first half of 2027.

items.title: Flight Centre investigating mass cyber breach
paras: Flight Centre says it is investigating a "significant" cyber breach. ( ABC News: Liz Pickering )
Customer data has been exposed in a cyber breach targeting a third-party accommodation system used by several of Flight Centre's booking agencies.
The travel agency says "unknown persons" accessed customers' basic travel information and a small number of passport details.
The company is warning customers to stay vigilant for unexpected emails or text messages about their bookings.
Australian travel agency Flight Centre is investigating a cyber breach it says exposed a significant number of customer records, including some passport details.

In a statement to the ASX on Thursday, the Brisbane-based travel giant reported it had discovered "unusual activity" within the third-party accommodation system used by several of its booking agencies.
These included Flight Centre, Travel Associates and Cruiseabout, as well as some independent agents.
Flight bookings and corporate travel bookings were not affected, the company said.

Early findings indicated "a significant number of customer records", comprising details such as names and some basic travel information, may have been accessed by "unknown persons", the travel agency said.
The company does not yet know how many customer records have actually been extracted.

A "very small percentage" of the compromised data included "limited passport details, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, or in rare cases health or mobility information", Flight Centre said.
Credit card, payment or banking details had not been affected at this stage.
Customers have been warned to exercise caution if they receive unexpected messages about their travel bookings. ( ABC News: Liz Pickering )

It is not clear exactly when the breach was discovered, but Flight Centre said it had responded by working with the third-party service to enhance its system security and contain the unusual activity.
The company said it was working with cybersecurity experts to understand the full "nature and extent" of the breach.

"FLT (Flight Centre Travel) is in the process of notifying the relevant authorities and has engaged external specialists to support in these investigations, including cyber security incident partner Mandiant," a statement to the ASX said.
Customers with existing accommodation bookings through Flight Centre's leisure brands can continue their travel plans without disruption, the company said.

Flight Centre is warning customers to be cautious of "unexpected emails, calls or messages" about their bookings, and to "not click on links, open attachments or share personal information, passwords or payment details in response".
The company apologised to affected customers, noting "that an incident like this can be unsettling".

Flight Centre is the latest Australian company to suffer a major security breach, following incidents at Origin this year and Qantas in 2025. Both Optus and Medibank also experienced mass breaches in 2022.
In June, a rogue OpenAI agent hacked into an Australian Medicare data portal , fuelling concerns about the existential risks posed by autonomous artificial intelligence.

items.title: Report finds Support at Home co-payments should be reviewed
paras: Clinicians should be able to override aged care algorithms assessing funding, the report has found. ( Getty: Resolution Productions )
The amount older Australia contribute to Support at Home services should be reviewed, a parliamentary committee has found.

A year after Labor's sweeping aged care changes took effect, the Senate committee into the Support at Home program has made 19 recommendations, including allowing clinicians to override algorithm outcomes.

Co-payments elderly Australians make towards the subsidised care they receive at home should be reviewed and clinicians should be able to override controversial assessment algorithms, a parliamentary committee has found.

A year on from the federal government's aged care overhaul, a Senate committee has recommended the Health Department review the amount elderly Australians pay towards their Support at Home services, such as cleaning, food preparation or gardening.

Senators from across the parliament also called on the government to "immediately" change the law to allow for humans to override "at the point of assessment" the algorithms used in the assessment process.

The Coalition and crossbenchers, including the Greens, have been highly critical of the government's Support at Home program and the two algorithms used to determine the level of funding someone requires and how quickly they should be given that money.

Controversially, the algorithms cannot be overridden by human clinicians , prompting the government to establish an "escalation pathway" so people in "exceptional circumstances" can have their outcomes reviewed.
After staunchly defending the algorithms as a way to improve consistency, the government also announced in October it would review the algorithms.
Under the changes that took effect in November last year, older people are required to contribute more to the non-clinical care they receive at home.
Recipients cover between 5 and 80 per cent of the service, depending on the type of help and whether or not they are a full or part pensioner.
Services like cleaning and meal preparation demand a higher contribution, compared to remedial or respite care.
It suggests reviewing how the assessment model impacts older older people with varying incomes and needs. ( ABC News: Patrick Stone )

But the committee recommended the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing review this model to assess the impacts on older people with varying incomes and needs, and to determine if co-payments "discourage timely access to care".
The committee was supposed to deliver a final report, but has instead made an interim report and extended the inquiry until November next year.
On that basis, Labor Senators said they did not intend to comment on the content and recommendations of the interim findings.
"[We] instead reserve our consideration of the work of the committee until the time it presents its final report to the Senate," Labor Senators said in additional comments.
Inquiry Chair and Greens spokesperson for older people, Senator Penny Allman-Payne, said Labor had "botched" the Support at Home program and added "baffling layers of bureaucracy and complexity".

"Not only are providers jacking up their prices, the system rations and denies care, systematically underassessing need and priority and creating artificial scarcity by withholding packages," she said.
Shadow Aged Care Minister Anne Ruston said many of the problems were either predictable or known to the government before the changes began.
"Labor dismissed them and now a Senate committee has confirmed every word," she said.
"The committee has backed what the Coalition has said from day one: an algorithm should never have the final say over an older person's care," Senator Ruston said.
"At a bare minimum, Labor must restore human override now, and stop short-changing older Australians with 60 per cent packages while hundreds of millions of dollars sit unspent," she said.
During Question Time on Thursday, Centre Alliance MP Rebekha Sharkie echoed criticism from Liberal Senator Anne Ruston earlier in the week about the government not spending its full aged care budget.
Ms Sharkie asked Aged Care Minister Sam Rae why Labor underspent by $1.4 billion last financial year.
Sam Rae says as of June 30, more than 390,000 people were on ongoing packages. ( ABC News: Dane Hirst )
"Ageing Australia stated they had capacity to deliver Support at Home to 30,000 additional older Australians," Ms Sharkie said.

Mr Rae said that was a "modest" part of the overall $44 billion budget, but nonetheless it had not been spent because providers were responding slower than anticipated to the need for more at-home packages and new residential beds.
"Since the Labor government was elected in 2022, we've effectively doubled the size of the aged care budget," Mr Rae said.
As of June 30, Mr Rae said more than 390,000 people were on ongoing packages, while more than 106,000 were waiting to receive their approved level of help.
According to data from earlier this year, more than 6,400 older Australians died while in the queue for their Support at Home funding.

Despite not securing the full $3 billion of savings the government was hoping to make from private health insurance rebate changes this week, Health Minister Mark Butler said Labor would still invest that full amount into aged care.

Share A A A Lakshmi Venu has filed a lawsuit against her billionaire father Venu Srinivasan seeking a “rightful share” in the family’s automobile-to-finance empire, escalating the fight over wealth at one of India’s oldest business dynasties.

Her petition in the Madras High Court demands a “fair and lawful partition” of assets held by her father’s branch of the TVS Group, according to a statement Wednesday. The family controls two-wheeler maker TVS Motor, parent TVS Holdings, auto components supplier Sundaram-Clayton, and shadow lender TVS Credit Services.

Lakshmi Venu’s feud with her father, Venu Srinivasan, underscores escalating fights among several Indian corporates around succession-related issues. Internet The lawsuit intensifies the battle for family wealth and follows Lakshmi’s November 16 legal notice to her father outlining her demands. The feud underscores an escalating fight among several Indian corporates around succession-related issues. Srinivasan is also a key figure in a separate power struggle at the Tata Group, where he serves as vice chairman of Tata Trusts, the charities that ultimately control the $US180-billion conglomerate.
Her father’s “reply reflects no change in his position and no recognition of her lawful rights,” Lakshmi said in the statement.

Venu Srinivasan is also a key figure in a separate power struggle at the Tata Group, where he serves as vice chairman of Tata Trusts, the charities that ultimately control the $US180-billion conglomerate. Bloomberg Srinivasan didn’t immediately respond to emailed queries.

Lakshmi argued last week that an earlier restructuring of the sprawling TVS empire divided businesses among different sides of the family but did not constitute a partition within the Venu Srinivasan family. She alleged that there was a concentration of beneficial interest in favour of her brother Sudarshan Venu, chairman and managing director at TVS Motor.

Her father’s lawyer has disputed that account, according to a report by Business Today . Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi said in an interview that the family reached written settlements in 2017, 2020 and 2024 covering both ownership and management. He called the latest challenge an attempt to reopen settlements that were entered into voluntarily.
The fight hinges, in part, on whether the agreements merely allocated control of businesses or also settled ownership of the underlying family wealth.

Lakshmi is also seeking access to records detailing the family’s assets, alleging the information has been withheld despite repeated requests, according to the statement. She turned to the court after efforts to reach a private settlement failed and her father rejected her claims, she said.

Her mother Mallika Srinivasan, chairwoman of tractor maker TAFE, has backed her daughter. Lakshmi has a legitimate claim to a share of the family assets equal to her brother’s, the statement quoted her as saying.
The lawsuit concerns ownership of family wealth and not the day-to-day operations of the companies, it said.
TVS Motor is valued at $US23.7 billion, while Sundaram-Clayton’s market capitalisation stood at $US247 million as of Wednesday.

items.title: RBI Bulletin – November 2026
paras: Today, the Reserve Bank released the November 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin. The Bulletin includes six speeches, four articles and current statistics. The four articles are: I. State of the Economy; II. Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict; III. Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review; and IV. Disentangling the Impact of US Monetary Policy on Indian Financial Markets: An Event Study Approach. I. State of the Economy Supply side challenges, elevated energy prices, and geopolitical uncertainty remain significant headwinds to the global economic outlook. Persistent inflationary pressures have led to synchronised monetary policy tightening across major central banks in the last three months. Pullback in AI-related stocks and elevated sovereign bond yields, despite some softening from multi-decade highs, remain a source of volatility in financial markets. Amidst uneven economic performance globally, the Indian economy stood out. High-frequency indicators of domestic economic activity showed resilience in October, underpinned by strong credit demand. Headline CPI inflation inched up, primarily driven by higher food inflation. With strong exports performance, the trade deficit narrowed in October as compared to corresponding month of the previous year. Equity markets rebounded supported by robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio inflows. Net inflows under ECB and NRI deposits also remained strong. II. Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict By Snehal S. Herwadkar, Ishu Thakur, Abhiruchi Rathi, Paras and Parul Arora This article examines how successive global shocks have reshaped the drivers of imported inflation in India. It constructs an import-intensity-weighted consumer price index (CPI) using item-level production, imports and exports data to assess the contribution of imported items to retail inflation. The analysis finds that food and fuel were the principal channels through which imported inflation impacted retail inflation during the COVID-19 pandemic as also during the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Precious metals became a key source of imported core inflation from 2025, while the West Asia conflict renewed crude oil-related pressures in 2026. Highlights: The import-intensity-weighted measure indicates that imported items account for 8.5 per cent of the new CPI basket (base 2024=100). Import intensity is highest for fuel and light, followed by food and beverages, and core components. Despite the small weight of imported items in CPI basket, it contributed around 18 per cent to the CPI headline inflation in October 2026. The West Asia conflict generated a sharper crude oil price shock than the Russia-Ukraine conflict. However, the pass-through to retail fuel prices in the current episode has been relatively lower, limiting the pressures on imported inflation. Higher precious metals prices emerged as another source of imported inflation since 2024. III. Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review By Monalisa Poali, Pallavi Pant, Abhyuday Harsh and Brijesh P This article assesses the performance of the non-banking financial company (NBFC) sector as at end-March 2026. Highlights: The NBFC sector continued to demonstrate double-digit y-o-y credit growth along with improvement in asset quality at end-March 2026. Industry and retail segment accounted for the largest component of NBFCs’ loan portfolio. Within retail loans, vehicle, gold and microfinance loans accounted for the largest share. Higher growth in retail loans at end-March 2026 is driven by rapid growth in advances to individuals against gold. IV. Disentangling the Impact of US Monetary Policy on Indian Financial Markets: An Event Study Approach By Mayank Gupta, Anishma Sebastian, Bhanu Pratap and Thangzason Sonna This article examines how information conveyed by the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcements is associated with Indian financial markets. It distinguishes between monetary news, which signals tighter US monetary conditions, and growth news, which reflects stronger US economic prospects. It also examines these associations across conventional and unconventional US monetary policy phases. Highlights: Increase in US G-sec yields driven by monetary news are associated with rupee depreciation, higher Indian 10-year government bond yields and lower Sensex returns. Growth news shows no statistically significant association with the Indian financial variables. The exchange rate and government bond yield are significantly associated with monetary news during both conventional and unconventional US monetary policy phases. Sensex returns are significantly associated with monetary news during the conventional phase. India VIX shows no statistically significant association with either monetary or growth news. The main findings remain broadly consistent across alternative model specifications and news-classification thresholds. The views expressed in the Bulletin articles are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1563

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
paras: Bog down Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming Detailed estimate going back to 1800 shows how much carbon is being liberated.

5 ... ... ... Credit: Muslianshah Masrie Credit: Muslianshah Masrie Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.

Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don’t digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO 2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO 2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO 2 . That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.

Many peatlands have been drained by digging ditches that let water flow out to repurpose the land for agriculture or other uses. That lowers the water level, supplying oxygen to the exposed peat and ringing the aerobic bacteria dinner bell. Methane emissions get turned down, and CO 2 emissions get turned way up.

The researchers used recent studies that measure gas emissions from peatlands to build a global model that estimated CO 2 and methane release as the water level drops. The two gases respond differently to a given drop in water level, and CO 2 in particular responds differently depending on where in the world the bog is located. Using reconstructions of water-level changes due to historical peatland drainage, the team ran their model starting in 1800.

The simplest way to represent the climate impact of both CO 2 and methane changes was to calculate the change in Earth’s energy budget—the strength of the greenhouse effect, in other words. They calculated the total effect in 2020 at about +83 milliwatts per square meter of the Earth’s surface from the CO 2 emissions, and about -9 milliwatts per square meter from the reduced methane emissions, for a total effect of +73 mW. That is 2.7 percent of the total human-caused change in Earth’s energy budget. (With the error bars on all these numbers, it’s 1.8–3.6 percent.)
Or to look at it another way, it means that around 4 percent of all the carbon that was buried in peatlands is now in the atmosphere.

Regionally, over half of the total CO 2 came from Europe, almost a quarter came from Southeast Asia, and only 14 percent came from North America. The timing is quite different, as well, with the contribution from Southeast Asia only jumping up in the last few decades.

Draining a peatland only starts the process of releasing carbon, though. So that means past land-use change will still be producing emissions in the future. To examine this, the researchers also ran their model forward to 2100.

If peatland water levels were simply held constant from 2020 on, the total change in Earth’s energy budget would nearly double, from 73 to 138 milliwatts per square meter by 2100. Moderate restoration of peatland water levels could reduce that growth, and ambitious restoration could even cause the effect to shrink slightly below its 2020 potency in their analysis. This is a process we can halt if we really want to.

But since rolling all the way back to the landscape of 1800 is unlikely, elevated emissions will continue for a long time. That makes this another part of the climate system where change plays out slowly, with long-term consequences.

items.title: From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices
paras: Our offices: Let us show you them From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices Our home offices range from tasteful to “please explain yourself.”

18 ... ... ... Credit: Aurich Lawson | Ars Staff Credit: Aurich Lawson | Ars Staff Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Ars Technica is a place that has always leaned into remote working. Since its beginnings in 1998, Ars has never had a single, central office—a setup that makes for a great commute to work, with little risk of getting stuck in traffic.

As Ars staffers step away from their desks for a few days to spend some time with family and friends, we wanted to give you a look inside our home offices. We’ve got all sorts of setups, tucked into basements, dens, spare bedrooms, apartment corners, and lofts. They run the gamut from minimalist “here’s my laptop and monitor” setups to “I really like collecting things.” Without any further ado, let’s dig in:

As an apartment dweller in New York City, I’ve usually set up my home work station in a small corner of my residence along with sometimes decamping for local cafes or coworking spaces. My current hodgepodge of equipment is probably on the minimal side compared to many members of the Ars team.

I’m usually multitasking on my basic monitor display and work laptop configuration, with the monitor sitting on a stack of several books (apologies in particular to Mary Beard’s excellent history of the Roman Republic, titled SPQR).

Accessories plugged into the work laptop include a simple Lekvey Ergonomic Mouse and a Logitech K380 keyboard that I’ve often brought along with me to public workspaces. Sometimes I’ll use the built-in Macbook Air keyboard, but I like having the laptop display elevated, whether I’m working at home or elsewhere.
My personal Apple M4 Macbook Air usually sits on the side, where I primarily use my old, battered pair of Sennheiser HD 518 headphones to listen to music during the work day.

I have a simple standing desk, but it’s not the easiest to change positions, so I wouldn’t recommend it for anyone who wants to adjust frequently. Whenever I’m sitting, I sometimes switch between a simple wooden chair from Ikea and a more ergonomic chair.

Aside from an assortment of coasters and a tea container turned pen holder, my desk also holds a painted dinosaur sculpture (courtesy of my young son) and two versions of the Spot It! Matching game (also for my son’s entertainment).

Last but not least, I have a pair of Powerblock dumbbells tucked under my work desk. I wouldn’t say they feature heavily in my work day, but they’re easily accessible if I have 15-20 minutes to spare.

Greetings from my basement hobbit hole! My desk sits across from a workbench area that was already here when we got the house. I have labeled drawers full of PC parts, tools, and cables accumulated over decades. The drawer organization was quite the upgrade over my previous solution of “chuck everything in unlabeled storage tubs.”

My current PC setup is an AceMagic W1 mini PC running Fedora, and a Blackview Intel N150 I keep on Windows for audio recording (PipeWire is fussy). The two are connected to my inputs and monitors via a KVM so I can switch back and forth at the press of a button.

The monitors are mismatched thrift finds. One is an HP, the other Sansui. The TV is a similar story—an old Samsung LCD that set me back $10 at the thrift store. I use it as a third monitor for watching PC streams. An Onn Android box is also connected, though it rarely earns its keep.

Below the TV sits a Lenovo ThinkSmart View, a repurposed B2B video-conference gadget modded to run LineageOS. It handles smart-home controls and tracks my solar production during the day. There’s also a Flashforge 5M printer in the corner, and the pegboard wall holds tools, Mega Man figures, and about 10 years’ worth of convention badges.

The back closet is the scary part: old consoles, spare drives, boards, and parts for every project I’ll get to “eventually.” The chair is a Dowinx gaming chair I grabbed on a Slickdeals whim—it’s fine, but I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone.

I’m something of an outlier at Ars, in that I use Windows most days. I’m no great lover of Windows 11, but I still use it thanks to years of computing inertia. My machine is custom, built in early 2024 with a Raptor Lake Core i7 (that thankfully did not fall victim to the overvolting bug) and an RTX 4070 Ti. It has long been my preference to build my own PC for gaming and work to ensure easier repairs and upgrades. Although with the prices of components being what they are, I hope all these parts last a very long time.

The primary monitor on the bottom is an Alienware ultrawide OLED. I got it for gaming, but it’s also a nice productivity display that gives me lots of room to keep windows visible. Above that, I have an Asus ProArt LCD calibrated in sRGB for photography work. I’ll get to the keyboard, but I do want to point out my preferred mouse, a Logitech MX Vertical. I have carpal tunnel issues, and this thing has been a lifesaver.

I believe organizing my desk before taking the photo would be a form of lying, so rest assured this is what it looks like on an average day. I have a few organizers to keep phones and various accessories from getting scattered around my Uplift sit-stand desk (seen here in sitting mode), which I quite like. The chair is a Herman Miller Aeron, which I don’t like as much. It’s fine and has plenty of adjustments, but the mesh is very hard. You should only buy one on sale, and if you do, get a cushion.

Above the desk are some Star Trek cross-stitches, courtesy of my talented wife. The dangling ’90s-era computer components are a mobile I put together many years ago, featuring a neat Intel i486 DEC socket board and some SDRAM.

I’m not a particularly neat person. My natural state is to have two or three projects half-exploded all over every surface: piles of 3D-printed prototypes, spools of wire, a soldering iron, laser-cut acrylic for a pinball project, the packaging from something I recently opened and need to sort through. Those aren’t random examples; that’s the contents of my workbench behind me on the opposite wall of my office as I type this. It’s a bit of a mess.

To combat that tendency, I make a concerted effort to keep the desk where I spend so many hours of the day calm and a place where I can focus. It doesn’t always last! But I’m always at least striving for it, and what I find helps is having a very intentional design where everything has a place.

My desk surface is made from rubberwood butcher block, on Flexispot motorized legs. I recently picked up another rubberwood slab to build the cantilevered shelf. The supports neatly tuck away my M1 Max Mac Studio, which is still a great little workhorse with 64 gigs of RAM, and my Arturia audio interface, which I use to record line-in sources like synthesizers.

On the left is a task lamp and a pen holder with six discrete holes. This fits in with the intentional design part: I have to pick the six things I want handy, and I can’t just pack it with more and more stuff. Currently that’s my Apple Pencil, a Pentel mechanical pencil, an Olfa mini snap-off blade knife, and a selection of three Pigma Micron pens in different line widths.

The right side holds an Aiyima 10th anniversary hi-fi stack: A20 amp, D20 DAC, and T20 pre-amplifier. The speakers are SVS Ultra Evolution Nanos. They’re sitting on the latest version of some 3D-printed stands I’ve been designing. I print them with hollow legs and then fill them with concrete for mass and stability.

Since I know Ryan is going to flex on everyone with his keyboard collection, I have to try my best to keep up with my daily driver. It’s a Percent Canoe v2 case, running Holy Panda switches modified with 63 gram SPRiT springs for a slightly lighter touch, and GMK Bento keycaps. This was a pandemic build project, and it has served me well since.

I used to run multiple monitors, but I’ve found that I don’t focus as well with them and prefer a singular spot to pay attention to. I’m using an Apple Studio Display because I’m very picky about pixel density. I opted to order it without the stand so I can run it on an ergo arm.

When I built the shelf for my desk, I fabricated a mounting bracket for the arm out of schedule 40 steel pipe and a 3D-printed sleeve that sits in a pocket CNC’d out. Since it sits flush on the underside, I don’t have to use a clamp that would extend down into the space where I keep my Mac and audio interface.

Aurich Lawson/Ars Technica Aurich’s iPad Pro doubles as a second monitor and graphic tablet. Aurich Lawson/Ars Technica When I need a secondary display, or I want to use my Apple Pencil in Photoshop or Illustrator, I use an iPad Pro. I used to have a dedicated Wacom monitor, but I find this much more convenient both in terms of space efficiency and ergonomics. If I’m not really leaning into hand drawing or lettering, I do most of my graphic work with a mouse, which is currently a Logitech MX Master 3S.

To wrap up the final items, the chair is an Aeron I bought new in 2003. I’ve had to repair it a few times over the years, but it’s either been things I consider wear items (wheels, armrests, gas cylinder) or Herman Miller has replaced under warranty. It was a big purchase for me at the time, but it’s ended up being a great investment. That’s Sophie draped over it, one of our four cats.

Tucked next to my desk, behind the subwoofer under the little side table, is my home server and networking gear. The server runs Unraid and is primarily used for my Jellyfin media collection and Home Assistant. Networking is a combination of Unifi and Eero, but at some point I’d like to ditch the Amazon gear and go fully native Unifi.

I spend a lot of time in my office. It’s not just a place to edit, write, and do other Ars-y things. It’s also my rehearsal space and a place to relax and unwind when I need some me-time. Long-time readers won’t be surprised to see Apple hardware front and center. I’ve been using Macs since college, and they’ve done alright by me ever since. items.title: Things I’m Grateful For In Tennis This Year
paras: It’s the tennis offseason (if you can even call it that), and at least for me, the brief time away from the sport always makes me appreciate it more when the Australian swing rolls around. But before I look ahead and count down the days until tennis destroys my sleep schedule once again, here’s what I’m grateful for in tennis this year.

This season, we saw plenty of players have incredible growth, either announcing themselves in the sport or reaching a higher level. The name that immediately stands out in that regard is certainly Rafael Jodar , who jumped from World No.
10 in his first full year on the ATP Tour. And it wasn’t just one or two big runs that did it—Jodar showed consistency throughout the year and plenty of promise as he continues to develop.

items.title: Marcel Granollers explains what so many people get wrong about Carlos Alcaraz which ‘blows him away’
paras: Carlos Alcaraz is one of the most famous athletes on the planet right now, and his stock stands to only get higher and higher as the years go by. After all, he is already one of tennis’ most affable and successful young superstars, poised to one day rival the achievements amassed by the Big Three.

The closer he gets to reaching such impossible heights, the more his profile will rise. However, despite being such a renowned public figure, the 23-year-old remains supremely humble and down to earth.

Where does Carlos Alcaraz now rank among the best players in tennis history? Alcaraz has already won seven Grand Slams and the ATP Finals at just 23 years old! Rafael Jodar recently discussed what Alcaraz was really like behind the scenes , insisting that he is the same off camera as he is when on it.

items.title: Mirra Andreeva’s 2026 Season Recap: Teen Prodigy No More
paras: Andreeva had announced herself in 2025 with back-to-back WTA 1000 titles in Dubai and Indian Wells, and the question hanging over her was whether that surge was a breakthrough or a blip. Four singles titles later — Adelaide, Linz, Roland Garros and the WTA Finals — the answer is emphatic.

Andreeva opened the year in style in Adelaide, falling behind 0-3 to Victoria Mboko in the final before reeling off nine straight games to win 6-3, 6-1. The hard-court spring that followed was bumpier: her title defences in Dubai and Indian Wells fizzled, the latter ending in a third-round loss to Katerina Siniakova.

Then came the clay, and with it, the best tennis of her life. She won Linz from a set down against Anastasia Potapova, 1-6 6-4 6-3; reached the Stuttgart semifinals (upsetting Iga Swiatek along the way); made the Madrid final; and then produced the defining fortnight of her career in Paris.

items.title: Flavio Cobolli claims he had one of his ‘best performances’ despite losing to the world number 139 in the Davis Cup
paras: Flavio Cobolli suffered more Davis Cup disappointment in Italy’s opening tie at the Davis Cup Finals.
Cobolli lost all three matches he played on his ATP Finals debut last week, but was hoping to bounce back at the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna, where Italy are three-time defending champions.

Italy were still able to make it through this tie after wins for Lorenzo Musetti and a deciding doubles win for Matteo Berrettini and Andrea Vavassori, and Cobolli was not actually too downcast about his own performance either. items.title: November 26, 1998: The day Pete Sampras secured the year-end No 1 ranking for a record sixth straight time
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to a big moment in tennis history.
On November 26, 1998, Pete Sampras set a new record by logging his sixth consecutive year-end No 1 ranking after playing a gruelling schedule post the US Open

On this day, November 26, 1998, Pete Sampras secured the year-end world No 1ranking for an unprecedented sixth consecutive time. Ironically, the news came when world No 2 Marcelo Rios pulled out during the ATP Tour World Championships, an announcement that was made on Pete’s day off. “Pistol Pete” was rewarded for his effort after he had played for six weeks without a break in order to finish the year at the top spot and break Jimmy Connors ’ record of five consecutive years as year-end world No 1.
items.impact: Sampras had triumphed four times at the US Open (1990, 1993, 1995, 1996) and twice at the Australian Open (1994, 1997), and was now only one title away from Roy Emerson’s record of 12 Grand Slam crowns.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
